submission.natural_language_explanation: L2/H1 is a pure previous-token head: on random sequences it puts 0.91 of its attention on t-1 (duplicate 0.00, induction 0.00) and writes that token's layer-2 value into the residual stream, so its strength |W_O(z - mean z)| at a position measures the token BEFORE it, not the token it sits on - in 'The map shows Yuri in the corner.' the piece 'ĠY' scores 0.00 and the next piece 'uri' 1.22, in 'methylglyoxal' 'Ġmethyl' scores 0.00, 'gly' 1.86, 'ox' 0.85, 'al' 0.60. Predict active (peak 1.2-3.3, well above the 0.83 line) when the token before the peak is an unusual, non-whole-word piece: any non-Latin-script byte piece (Arabic, Greek, Cyrillic, Devanagari, Bengali, Thai: 1.2-2.1), a fragment of a multi-piece word or name that is not itself a common English word ('ĠSal' 1.16, 'ĠBr' 1.86, 'Ġmethyl' 1.86, 'ost' 1.99, 'ĠSh'/'ĠY'/'ĠZ' 1.2-1.9), or a piece of an all-caps identifier ('IN' 1.58, 'JA' 1.84, '_' 0.39); predict weak, near or just over the line (0.4-1.4), after a whole ordinary English word, including whole proper names ('John Smith met Mary Jones at the inn on the hill.' peaks at 0.65) and common content words ('short' 1.41, 'light' 1.12, 'cat' 1.05, 'composer' 0.12); predict inactive (0.0-0.15) only for text built entirely from the ~200 most frequent English tokens with no content noun, adjective, digit or foreign piece ('It is not that I do not want to, it is that I cannot.' 0.00; six such sentences 0.00-0.14), for space-separated digits ('100 200 300 400 500 600 700' 0.00) and for comma-separated lists of single common words ('Trees, rivers, mountains.' 0.00).

rival_explanations: The head is a rare-token detector at the current position, not a previous-token copier: it should fire on the unusual piece itself, so 'ĠY' in 'Yuri', 'Ġmethyl' in 'methylglyoxal' and 'ĠN' in 'NINJA_URL' should be as strong as the pieces after them.

The trigger is tokenizer fragmentation alone, not rarity or script: any word split into three or more pieces should fire on all its later pieces ('establ' and 'ishment' in antidisestablishmentarianism, 'ox' and 'al' in methylglyoxal, 'work' and 'able' in unworkable), and no single-piece word should ever fire.

The trigger is the proper-noun word class that the confound profile flags (PROPN tokens are 46% active): the head should fire after any proper noun or place name, so 'John', 'Smith', 'Mary' and 'London' should be as strong as the Shostakovich fragments.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Another all-common-token question with no content noun, adjective, digit or foreign piece, the class the hypothesis predicts scores 0.0-0.15.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We will not do it now. It is not what we want, and it is not what they want, so it will not be done.
adversarial_test_results.detail: All-common-token text across a sentence boundary, testing that a period plus a whole common word still does not make the retrospection fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is what it is, and it is not what it was, but it is what it will be, and that is all it is.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Repeated all-common-token clause with no content word, testing the hypothesis's inactive class rather than the zero duplicate-head score.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Longer comma-separated common-word list drawn from single-token nouns, a paraphrase of the hypothesis's 'Trees, rivers, mountains.' zero case.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Run, walk, jump, swim, climb, rest, wait, watch, listen, speak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Well, no, it is not so, but it is not that it is not, is it, and that is that.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Punctuated all-common-token sentence testing that commas and periods, which the hypothesis scores 0.00, do not create a retrospective peak.
